topic: phase retrieval from physical photon counts with a complete POVM and charged total photon budget
overall_status: exact count-law derivations proved; conditional random-frame upper and quantum lower match in order; implementation and nuisance robustness unresolved

claims.statement: For a normalized complete POVM with outcome law p(x), N fixed photon copies have counts Multinomial(N,p(x)); a Poissonian source with mean N has independent counts Pois(N p_j(x)). The independent-Poisson total is Pois(N), not N per outcome. Their exact Bhattacharyya affinities are respectively (sum_j sqrt(p_j(x)p_j(y)))^N and exp[-N/2 ||sqrt(p(x))-sqrt(p(y))||_2^2].
assumptions: All outcomes of a complete POVM are recorded, including loss/no-click/herald/failure outcomes when present.
The state x is normalized, so sum_j p_j(x)=1 for every hypothesis.
Fixed-N and Poissonized source models are kept distinct; in the Poissonized case N is expected total input photons.
claims.status: direct exact derivation from multinomial and Poisson mass functions
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical splitting/Poissonization and Hellinger affinity; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: N total incident photons across all outcomes and settings; a setting label is part of the POVM outcome when settings are randomized.
claims.falsifier: A count model in which the stated outcomes are not conditionally independent given a Poisson total or not multinomial given fixed N.

claims.statement: For two known states under a fixed calibrated frame, the Neyman-Pearson statistic uses all recorded counts: under fixed N it is sum_j K_j log(p_j(x1)/p_j(x0)); under independent Poisson counts with means N p_j it is sum_j Y_j log(p_j(x1)/p_j(x0)) because the normalized-state rate correction vanishes. With known additive background c_j the full Poisson log-likelihood ratio instead uses means N p_j(x)+c_j, including the compensator term. A rare prior changes the decision threshold, not the count budget.
assumptions: The two hypotheses and measurement probabilities are known.
All outcomes and setting labels are retained.
Background means, if present, are known for the displayed likelihood; their calibration cost is additional.
claims.status: direct likelihood-ratio derivation; implements the strongest simple-hypothesis test for the same fixed measurement
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical Neyman-Pearson testing; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: N fixed incident photons or expected N photons in the Poissonized experiment, across all outcomes/settings; background calibration exposure is separate.
claims.falsifier: A mismatch between the stated likelihood ratio and the full multinomial or independent-Poisson outcome law.

claims.statement: Let G be an m-by-d complex standard Gaussian matrix, S=G*G, and B=G S^{-1/2}. Conditional on Xia-Xu-Xu's Theorem 4.3 event and their Lemma 4.2 singular-value event, B*B=I and its rank-one POVM E_j=b_j b_j* satisfies || |Bx|-|By| ||_2 >= ell d_phi(x,y) uniformly, with ell >= (1/beta0-delta)/sqrt(1+rho), beta0=sqrt(4/(4-pi)), 0<delta<0.05, 0<rho<1. The event probability is at least 1-4 exp(-c2 delta^2 m)-2 exp(-c1 rho^2 m), provided m is at least the source's implicit constant times max{log(1/delta) delta^-2 d, rho^-2 d}.
assumptions: Complex standard Gaussian entries have real and imaginary variances 1/2.
m >= d so S is invertible almost surely.
d_phi(x,y)=min_|omega|=1 ||x-omega y||_2; magnitude stability is global, including non-unit arguments in the source theorem.
The theorem's universal constants c1,c2 and implicit sample-size constants are not numerically specified.
claims.status: internally derived from primary random-Gaussian magnitude stability plus Gram concentration; no external proof review
claims.novelty_boundary: The Gaussian modulus theorem is published prior work; polar-normalization transfer to a Parseval one-photon POVM is an elementary reconstruction, not priority-cleared novelty.
claims.costs: m detector outcomes, one outcome per incident photon, N photons total; calibration and physical realization of B are unpriced.
claims.falsifier: A flaw in the source lower-modulus event, the polar normalization, or the singular-value transfer inequality.

claims.statement: For a known Parseval POVM with global magnitude lower modulus ell, the global Hellinger minimum-distance fit xhat minimizing ||sqrt(Y/N)-|Bz||_2 over unit z under independent Y_j~Pois(N p_j(x)) satisfies sup_x E_x[d_phi(xhat,x)^2] <= 4m/(N ell^2). For exactly N photons and K~Multinomial(N,p(x)), replacing Y/N by K/N sharpens this to 4(m-1)/(N ell^2).
assumptions: No additive background, detector mismatch, or unmodeled loss; such mechanisms must be included in the full outcome law and the bound rederived.
The frame B and all outcome probabilities are known/calibrated.
The estimator is a global minimum-distance solution; no polynomial-time solver guarantee is asserted.
In the Poisson model N is the expected total count; in the multinomial model N is the fixed total count.
claims.status: internally proved from a coordinate square-root multinomial variance bound, global fit inequality, and modulus
claims.novelty_boundary: Generic Hellinger minimum-distance reasoning is classical; no new statistical estimator class is claimed.
claims.costs: Expected squared phase distance versus N fixed incident photons. A finite epsilon-net implementation is exponential in d; frame generation, calibration, computation, and hardware cost remain separate.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to E( sqrt(Y_j/N)-sqrt(p_j) )^2 <= 1/N for p_j>0, the corresponding multinomial bound E( sqrt(K_j/N)-sqrt(p_j) )^2 <= (1-p_j)/N, the fit triangle inequality, or the assumed ell modulus.

claims.statement: For estimating a Haar-uniform unknown pure d-dimensional state from N identical copies, any measurement-estimator, including arbitrary collective measurements, has average squared phase-distance risk at least (d-1)/(N+d), because optimal average fidelity is (N+1)/(N+d) and d_phi^2=2(1-c)>=1-c^2.
assumptions: The unknown input is genuinely N copies of the same pure d-dimensional state.
Risk is averaged over Haar prior; the resulting lower bound also lower-bounds worst-case risk.
d_phi is the phase-invariant Euclidean distance between normalized pure state vectors.
claims.status: primary theorem translated exactly to the squared phase-distance loss
claims.novelty_boundary: Bruß-Macchiavello 1999 is established quantum state-estimation theory; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: N copies/photons, with no free collective measurement apparatus assumed in physical comparison; theorem gives an information-theoretic bound even allowing collective measurements.
claims.falsifier: An estimator with Haar-average fidelity exceeding (N+1)/(N+d) under the same N-copy pure-state model.

claims.statement: If a family of complex random Parseval POVMs has m=Theta(d) and a uniform lower magnitude modulus ell bounded below by a positive constant, then the global Hellinger estimator has uniform expected squared phase risk O(d/N), while the quantum Haar-average lower bound is Omega(d/N) for N much larger than d. Thus N=Theta(d/epsilon^2) is supported in order for mean-squared phase error epsilon^2 under this ideal model.
assumptions: Fixed positive ell and linear outcome count m=Theta(d); the source theorem has hidden constants in m and failure probability.
Known normalized pure state family, known frame, zero background and no loss.
Expected-risk criterion; Markov conversion to a 1-zeta high-probability guarantee costs an additional 1/zeta factor.
The construction does not imply efficient optimization or physically free frame calibration.
claims.status: conditional order-match proved; finite constants and practical implementation unresolved
claims.novelty_boundary: Order follows from known Gaussian frame stability, a direct Parseval transfer and Hellinger fitting, and known optimal quantum state estimation; not a novelty or hardware-advantage claim.
claims.costs: m output channels and N total photons; also charge all frame calibration, preparation, readout, setting, ancilla, and computation resources in a deployment comparison.
claims.falsifier: Failure of the stipulated modulus event, a corrected MDE upper bound, or a weaker/stronger lower-bound interpretation under the precise loss and prior.

claims.statement: For a unit-row complex projective 2-design of m rows used as the POVM E_j=(d/m)u_j u_j*, the previous raw-intensity lower constant L^2=m/[2d(d+1)] implies ||sqrt(p(x))-sqrt(p(y))||_2 >= ||xx*-yy*||_* / [2 sqrt(2(d+1))], and hence independent-Poisson affinity <= exp[-N ||xx*-yy*||_*^2/(16(d+1))].
assumptions: Equal-weight projective 2-design, normalized pure states, all m outcomes included.
Uses the internally reconstructed raw-intensity law in ../nonlinear_inverse/FINAL_REPORT.md.
No additive background or loss.
claims.status: direct conversion of predecessor result; correct but dimension-looser than random Parseval magnitude stability for state-vector phase distance
claims.novelty_boundary: Classical projective designs plus the predecessor report's condition-number corollary; no new design theorem.
claims.costs: At least d^2 nonzero scalar outcomes are necessary to attain the predecessor's exact complex beta=2 optimum; physical implementation/calibration unpriced.
claims.falsifier: A flaw in the stated raw lower constant, POVM normalization, or amplitude-product inequality.

claims.statement: Dirksen-Krahmer-Romer-Salanevich Theorem 5 proves a real Gaussian-row Poisson spectral recovery guarantee for m>=n log n with relative squared phase error <=2 C_beta(1+C_hat_beta/alpha) log(m) sqrt(log(n)) sqrt(n/m) and success probability >=1-n^-beta-m exp(-c_beta n)-m^-beta, where alpha=||x||^2 and constants are absolute but unspecified. Expected total counts before conditioning on the design equal m alpha.
assumptions: Real x in R^n; independent standard Gaussian sensing vectors a_i.
Independent count observations y_i~Pois(|<a_i,x>|^2), no additive background.
Estimator is the leading eigenvector of m^-1 sum_i y_i a_i a_i^T, scaled to norm squared alpha.
Random unnormalized row model, not one normalized POVM or fixed-total-N multinomial counts.
claims.status: source-reported theorem checked against primary arXiv text; no independent proof audit
claims.novelty_boundary: Published direct Poisson phase-retrieval prior art; not a theorem for the present normalized POVM model.
claims.costs: Charge expected total count m alpha across every row, not alpha per row as if settings were free.
claims.falsifier: Mismatch in the primary theorem statement, model, probability bound, or expected total count calculation.

claims.statement: For independent output counts with known additive background means c_j and signal means N p_j(x), the exact Poisson affinity is exp[-(1/2) sum_j (sqrt(N p_j(x)+c_j)-sqrt(N p_j(y)+c_j))^2].
assumptions: Background means are known and fixed across compared states.
All outcomes are retained and the output counts are independent Poisson variables.
Calibration cost for c_j is not included in this formula and must be charged separately.
claims.status: direct exact derivation; no robustness theorem for estimated backgrounds claimed
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard Poisson Hellinger identity; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: N signal photons plus all background calibration exposure, detector dark-count estimation, and readout cost.
claims.falsifier: A count law not equal to independent Poisson with the stated means.

unknown: Numerical constants for the random-frame sample-size threshold and failure exponent in Xia-Xu-Xu.
Polynomial-time global solution of the Hellinger minimum-distance estimator for the random Parseval frame.
Uniform stability and optimal risk constants with uncertain background, frame calibration error, dark counts, losses, saturation, or heralding.
Whether any one-copy rank-one POVM attains the exact quantum minimax constant for phase retrieval under the stated risk.
Physical optical-network, ancilla, calibration, control, and processor energy needed to implement the random Parseval POVM and its estimator.
Any experimental advantage over the best equally informed calibrated Poisson maximum-likelihood estimator.
